# function: console_address

Joins a console host and a console port into `host:port`, for example `console_address("127.0.0.1", gns3_node.r1.console)` gives `127.0.0.1:5000`. An IPv6 host is bracketed (`[::1]:5000`). The host must not be empty and the port must be between 1 and 65535.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Provider functions need the provider in required_providers.
terraform {
  required_providers {
    gns3 = {
      source  = "JerryBalmer1/gns3"
      version = "~> 0.3"
    }
  }
}

resource "gns3_project" "lab" {
  name = "tf-example-console-address"
}

data "gns3_template" "vpcs" {
  name = "VPCS"
}

resource "gns3_node" "pc1" {
  project_id  = gns3_project.lab.project_id
  template_id = data.gns3_template.vpcs.template_id
  name        = "PC1"
}

# "127.0.0.1:5000", ready for telnet.
output "pc1_console" {
  value = provider::gns3::console_address("127.0.0.1", gns3_node.pc1.console)
}
```

## Signature

<!-- signature generated by tfplugindocs -->
```text
console_address(host string, console number) string
```

## Arguments

<!-- arguments generated by tfplugindocs -->
1. `host` (String) Host name or IP address of the console, usually the GNS3 server host. Must not be empty.
1. `console` (Number) Console TCP port, such as a node's `console`. Must be between 1 and 65535.
